newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate down.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weaker late, interbank rate down.

text.p: The Thai baht was down sharply against the dollar in late trade on Tuesday due to plentiful liquidity in the banking system, dealers said.
"Local banks were heavily buying the dollar. They don't want to hold the baht right now," said one dealer at a European bank.
The baht was traded at 25.985/25.990 to the dollar late compared with 25.972/25.977 in the morning.
Offshore players in Singapore and Hong Kong also bought dollars to square positions ahead of their long weekend, the dealer said. Hong Kong and Singapore will be closed on Friday.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 6.75-7.00 percent late from 7.50-8.00 percent on high liquidity, dealers said.
Dealers said the ample money supply stems from the gradual entry of some funds from the Government Pension Fund (GPF) which is scheduled to be launched this Thursday.
The market expects about 80 billion baht ($3 billion) Government Pension Fund (GPF) would enter the financial system after the launch.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 7.50/8.50 satangs per dollar late against 7.25/8.25 early.
